claim: Bacterial flotillins are important factors for membrane fluidity homeostasis.
source: We show here that bacterial flotillins are important factors for membrane fluidity homeostasis.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a main finding of the study.

claim: Loss of flotillins leads to a decrease in membrane fluidity.
source: Loss of flotillins leads to a decrease in membrane fluidity that in turn leads to alterations in MreB dynamics and, as a consequence, in peptidoglycan synthesis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by Laurdan microscopy data showing increased GP values in flotillin mutants.

claim: Loss of flotillins leads to alterations in MreB dynamics.
source: Loss of flotillins leads to a decrease in membrane fluidity that in turn leads to alterations in MreB dynamics and, as a consequence, in peptidoglycan synthesis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by TIRF microscopy data showing reduced MreB patch mobility.

claim: Loss of flotillins leads to alterations in peptidoglycan synthesis.
source: Loss of flotillins leads to a decrease in membrane fluidity that in turn leads to alterations in MreB dynamics and, as a consequence, in peptidoglycan synthesis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by HADA and Van-FL labeling showing accumulation at division septa.

claim: Alterations caused by loss of flotillins are reverted when membrane fluidity is restored by a chemical fluidizer.
source: These alterations are reverted when membrane fluidity is restored by a chemical fluidizer.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data showing benzyl alcohol treatment restores normal cell morphology and MreB dynamics.

claim: Addition of flotillin increases membrane fluidity of liposomes in vitro.
source: In vitro, the addition of a flotillin increases membrane fluidity of liposomes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by solid-state NMR data showing decreased order parameters.

claim: Flotillins are required for direct control of membrane fluidity rather than for the formation of protein complexes via direct protein-protein interactions.
source: Our data support a model in which flotillins are required for direct control of membrane fluidity rather than for the formation of protein complexes via direct protein-protein interactions.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, supported by multiple lines of evidence including NMR data and lack of changes in PBP oligomerization.

claim: The shape of a bacterium is predominantly defined by the structure of its peptidoglycan.
source: The shape of a bacterium is predominantly defined by the structure of its peptidoglycan.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: In rod-shaped bacteria, peptidoglycan synthesis is thought to be mediated by two protein assemblies, the elongasome and the divisome.
source: In rod-shaped bacteria, peptidoglycan synthesis is thought to be mediated by two protein assemblies, the elongasome and the divisome, that synthesise peptidoglycan along the long axis and across the division plane of the cell, respectively (Typas et al., 2012; Zhao et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: SEDS proteins can perform glycosyl transferase reactions.
source: These include SEDS (Shape, Elongation, Division and Sporulation) proteins that can perform glycosyl transferase reactions (Cho et al., 2016; Meeske et al., 2016; Taguchi et al., 2019)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Inward membrane curvature serves as a localisation trigger for MreB and the elongasome.
source: Inward membrane curvature serves as a localisation trigger for MreB and the elongasome, and enhanced local synthesis at bulges straightens out the membrane sufficient to convert spherical cells to a rod shape (Hussain et al., 2018; Ursell et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: In Bacillus subtilis, the motion of MreB along the membrane is associated with elongasome activity.
source: In Bacillus subtilis, the motion of MreB along the membrane is associated with elongasome activity (Domínguez-Escobar et al., 2011; Garner et al., 2011)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The velocity of MreB patches is related to growth rate.
source: the velocity of MreB patches is related to growth rate (Billaudeau et al., 2017)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: MreB localises to and organises regions of increased membrane fluidity (RIF).
source: Interestingly, MreB localises to and organises regions of increased membrane fluidity (RIF) (Strahl et al., 2014)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: LipidII favours a more fluid membrane and promotes local membrane disorder.
source: which in turn is linked to the presence of LipidII, which favours a more fluid membrane and promotes local membrane disorder (Ganchev et al., 2006; Witzke et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Inhibition of LipidII synthesis results in a dissolution of membrane structures observed with the dye FM 4–64 and release of MreB from the membrane.
source: Inhibition of LipidII synthesis by genetic or chemical means results in a dissolution of membrane structures observed with the dye FM 4–64 and release of MreB from the membrane (Domínguez-Escobar et al., 2011; Garner et al., 2011; Muchová et al., 2011; Schirner et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Functional membrane microdomains (FMMs) are thought to be organised by the bacterial flotillin proteins.
source: These so-called functional membrane microdomains (FMMs) are thought to be organised by the bacterial flotillin proteins
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a hypothesis from the literature.

claim: FMMs are enriched in isoprenoid lipids.
source: These so-called functional membrane microdomains (FMMs) are thought to be organised by the bacterial flotillin proteins, are enriched in isoprenoid lipids (García-Fernández et al., 2017; López and Kolter, 2010)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: FMMs can be found in Detergent Resistant Membrane (DRM) fractions of the membrane.
source: and can be found in so-called Detergent Resistant Membrane (DRM) fractions of the membrane.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: FMMs have been linked to protein secretion, biofilm formation, competence and cell morphology.
source: Since the formulation of the FMM hypothesis, FMMs have been linked to many processes, such as protein secretion, biofilm formation, competence and cell morphology (Mielich-Süss and Lopez, 2015; Mielich-Süss et al., 2013; Bach and Bramkamp, 2013; Dempwolff et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Analysis of the protein content of Bacillus subtilis DRMs identified several PBPs, MreC and other proteins involved in cell wall metabolism as well as the two flotillins, FloA and FloT.
source: Cell morphology defects are linked to cell wall synthesis, and analysis of the protein content of Bacillus subtilis DRMs identified several PBPs, MreC and other proteins involved in cell wall metabolism as well as the two flotillins, FloA and FloT (López and Kolter, 2010; Bach and Bramkamp, 2013; Yepes et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: FloA is constitutively expressed.
source: FloA is constitutively expressed, whereas FloT is expressed primarily during stationary growth, cell wall stress and sporulation (Schneider et al., 2015a; Huang et al., 1999; Nicolas et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: FloT is expressed primarily during stationary growth, cell wall stress and sporulation.
source: FloA is constitutively expressed, whereas FloT is expressed primarily during stationary growth, cell wall stress and sporulation (Schneider et al., 2015a; Huang et al., 1999; Nicolas et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Super resolution microscopy showed that the flotillins and other proteins found in DRMs do not colocalise and have different dynamics.
source: Super resolution microscopy showed that the flotillins and other proteins found in DRMs do not colocalise and have different dynamics (Dempwolff et al., 2016)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The hypothesis has been put forward that FMMs/flotillins form a platform for the formation of functional protein oligomers.
source: Recently, the hypothesis has been put forward that FMMs/flotillins form a platform for the formation of functional protein oligomers, as work in Staphylococcus aureus showed that multimerisation of Type 7 secretion systems and PBP2a depends on FMMs (Lopez and Koch, 2017; García-Fernández et al., 2017; Mielich-Süss et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: At high growth rates, flotillins control membrane fluidity in a manner that is critical for peptidoglycan synthesis and MreB dynamics.
source: Our results show that, at high growth rates, flotillins control membrane fluidity in a manner that is critical for peptidoglycan synthesis and MreB dynamics, but have no effect on PBP oligomerisation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a main finding of the study.

claim: Flotillins have no effect on PBP oligomerisation.
source: Our results show that, at high growth rates, flotillins control membrane fluidity in a manner that is critical for peptidoglycan synthesis and MreB dynamics, but have no effect on PBP oligomerisation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a main finding of the study.

claim: The ΔfloAT strain shows an increase in median cell length compared to wild type.
source: We did not observe striking shape defects but did see an increase in median cell length and distribution of cell lengths in the absence of flotillins (Figure 1A,G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Figure 1G showing cell length distributions.

claim: The ΔfloAT strain shows a significant accumulation of peptidoglycan synthesis stains at division septa.
source: This revealed a significant accumulation of peptidoglycan synthesis stains at division septa in the ΔfloAT strain (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Figure 1A-C showing HADA and Van-FL labeling.

claim: FM4-64, Nile-Red and DiI-C12 accumulate at the septa in the ΔfloAT strain.
source: Again, the stains accumulated at the septa in the ΔfloAT strain, which also showed some accumulation of FM4-64 and DiI-C12 in patches, suggesting that the more fluid regions of the membrane are coalescing into larger regions (Figure 1A,D–F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Figure 1A,D-F showing membrane dye labeling.

claim: There is no difference between the thicknesses of the septa between the wild type and ΔfloAT strain.
source: Inspection of the septa by electron microscopy revealed that there was no difference between the thicknesses of the septa between the wild type and ΔfloAT strain, ruling out that the increase in signal was due to formation of thicker septa (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by electron microscopy data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Growing cells at a sublethal concentration of fosfomycin results in bulging cells and some lysis, which is exacerbated in the ΔfloAT strain.
source: This was confirmed by growing cells at a sublethal concentration of fosfomycin, which limits synthesis of LipidII (Kahan et al., 1974), but that does not impact growth rate at the concentration used. This resulted in bulging cells and some lysis, which was exacerbated in the ΔfloAT strain (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1F,G.

claim: LB-grown cells lacking flotillins display an increased generalised polarisation (GP), indicative of an overall increase in ordered lipid packing in the membrane.
source: LB-grown cells lacking flotillins displayed an increased generalised polarisation (GP) (Bach and Bramkamp, 2013), indicative of an overall increase in ordered lipid packing in the membrane
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Laurdan microscopy data in Figure 3.

claim: The effect of flotillins on membrane ordering completely disappears when cells are grown on SMM.
source: but the effect of flotillins on membrane ordering completely disappeared when cells were grown on SMM (Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Laurdan microscopy data in Figure 3.

claim: Overall, lipid order is increased in cells grown on SMM compared to LB.
source: Overall, lipid order was increased in cells grown on SMM compared to LB (Figure 3)
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Laurdan microscopy data in Figure 3.

claim: The absence of PBP1 has no significant effect on membrane fluidity.
source: whereas the absence of PBP1 had no significant effect on membrane fluidity, also not when combined with flotillin deletions (Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Laurdan microscopy data in Figure 3.

claim: The ratios of C17/C15 side chains and iso/anteiso fatty acids are identical for wild type and ΔfloAT strains grown on LB.
source: The changes in lipid ordering were not due to changes in the overall fatty acid composition of the membranes - the ratios of C17/C15 side chains and iso/anteiso fatty acids, which are indicative of fluidity (Strahl et al., 2014), were identical for wild type and ΔfloAT strains grown on LB
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by fatty acid composition data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The addition of benzyl alcohol increases membrane fluidity to similar extents in the wildtype and the mutant strains.
source: Notably, the addition of benzyl alcohol increased membrane fluidity to similar extents in the wildtype and the mutant strains (see Figure 3C)
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Laurdan microscopy data in Figure 3C.

claim: Benzyl alcohol does not affect the growth rates of the strains.
source: but did not affect the growth rates of the strains (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by growth curve data in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The increase in membrane fluidity by benzyl alcohol restores normal cell length and normal peptidoglycan synthesis patterns to the pbp1/floA/floT strain.
source: The increase in membrane fluidity restored normal cell length and normal peptidoglycan synthesis patterns to the pbp1/floA/floT strain (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by microscopy data in Figure 2C.

claim: MreB patch mobility is higher in cells grown on LB than in cells grown on SMM.
source: Analysis of the movement of a fully functional mRFPruby-MreB fusion (Domínguez-Escobar et al., 2011) by time lapse TIRF (Total Internal Reflection Fluorescence) microscopy, confirmed that MreB patch mobility is higher in cells grown on LB than in cells grown on SMM
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by TIRF microscopy data in Figure 4.

claim: In the absence of flotillins, MreB patch mobility is notably decreased in cells grown on LB.
source: Strikingly, in the absence of flotillins, MreB patch mobility was notably decreased in cells grown on LB
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by TIRF microscopy data in Figure 4.

claim: In SMM grown cells, MreB patch mobility is independent of the presence of flotillins.
source: while in SMM grown cells MreB patch mobility was independent of the presence of flotillins (Figure 4, Figure 4—videos 3 and 4).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by TIRF microscopy data in Figure 4.

claim: Fluidising the membrane with benzyl alcohol almost completely restores MreB mobility in LB grown cells.
source: Fluidising the membrane with benzyl alcohol, which does not alter the growth rate, almost completely restored MreB mobility in LB grown cells (Figure 4, Figure 4—videos 5 and 6).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by TIRF microscopy data in Figure 4.

claim: FloT decreases the spectral width of the 2H quadrupolar splitting, reflecting an increase in motion on the atomic scale.
source: FloT decreases the spectral width of the 2H quadrupolar splitting, reflecting an increase in motion on the atomic scale (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by solid-state NMR data in Figure 5B.

claim: FloT significantly decreases the order parameter SCD along the entire acyl chain.
source: Strikingly, FloT has an important impact on the order parameter along the entire acyl chain. It is remarkable that the protein significantly decreases the order parameter SCD, reaching even the inner carbon atoms of the acyl chain, indicating a different packing behaviour and increased membrane fluidity upon interaction with FloT (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by solid-state NMR data in Figure 5B.

claim: The strong fluidising effect described for FloT is notably different from the effects other proteins have when reconstituted into liposomes.
source: The strong fluidising effect described for FloT is notably different from the effects other proteins have when reconstituted into liposomes, such as plant remorins (Legrand et al., 2019) or the membrane binding peptide of the nonreceptor tyrosine kinase Src (Scheidt and Huster, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citations.

claim: Upon interactions with FloT the lamellar phase remains intact with formation of a few smaller objects.
source: Upon interactions with FloT the lamellar phase remains intact with formation of a few smaller objects, indicating that the overall liposome structure is not affected and that its phase is maintained (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by 31P NMR data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Flotillins play a direct role in controlling membrane fluidity.
source: Our data provide evidence that flotillins play a direct role in controlling membrane fluidity and that membrane fluidity is critical for peptidoglycan synthesis at certain growth conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a main conclusion of the study.

claim: Membrane fluidity is critical for peptidoglycan synthesis at certain growth conditions.
source: Our data provide evidence that flotillins play a direct role in controlling membrane fluidity and that membrane fluidity is critical for peptidoglycan synthesis at certain growth conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a main conclusion of the study.

claim: In vitro, flotillins enhance the fluidity of a model membrane.
source: In vitro, flotillins enhance the fluidity of a model membrane
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by solid-state NMR data.

claim: In vivo, the membranes of fast growing flotillin-mutant cells are less fluid even though the fatty acid composition in these cells is identical.
source: and in vivo, the membranes of fast growing flotillin-mutant cells are less fluid even though the fatty acid composition in these cells is identical.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by Laurdan microscopy and fatty acid composition data.

claim: The effect of flotillins on membrane fluidity is direct, through a change in the packing behaviour of the lipids.
source: Therefore, we propose that the effect of flotillins on membrane fluidity is direct, through a change in the packing behaviour of the lipids resulting in an efficient separation of states of liquid ordered and disordered lipid domains in the membrane bilayer (Bach and Bramkamp, 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a proposed mechanism, supported by data and a citation.

claim: Membrane fluidity is not solely a function of temperature, but also of growth conditions.
source: We found that membrane fluidity is not solely a function of temperature, but also of growth conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by Laurdan microscopy data comparing LB and SMM growth.

claim: In fast-growing cells on rich medium, flotillin-mediated control of membrane fluidity is critical and sufficient to allow essential membrane bound processes, such as peptidoglycan synthesis, to proceed normally.
source: We propose that in fast-growing cells on rich medium, flotillin-mediated control of membrane fluidity is critical and sufficient to allow essential membrane bound processes, such as peptidoglycan synthesis, to proceed normally.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a proposed model.

claim: A sufficiently fluid membrane is necessary for the efficient recruitment and movement of MreB.
source: A sufficiently fluid membrane is necessary for the efficient recruitment and movement of MreB, and provides a more favourable environment for the peptidoglycan precursor LipidII (Hussain et al., 2018; Ursell et al., 2014; Schirner et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: Modulation of either MreBCD or PBP1 levels is sufficient to alter the shape of B. subtilis cells.
source: It has recently been shown that modulation of either MreBCD or PBP1 levels is sufficient to alter the shape of B. subtilis cells (Dion et al., 2019)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: In the absence of flotillins, the activity of the MreBCD component is strongly reduced.
source: In the absence of flotillins, the activity of the MreBCD component is strongly reduced – as evidenced by the reduction of MreB speed
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by TIRF microscopy data.

claim: In the absence of flotillins, the overall rigidity of the membrane is increased.
source: and the overall rigidity of the membrane is increased.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by Laurdan microscopy data.

claim: The reduction in elongasome activity is compensated by increased peptidoglycan synthesis activity around division sites in flotillin mutants.
source: Our data indicate that the reduction in elongasome activity, which does not impact the growth rate itself, is compensated by increased peptidoglycan synthesis activity around division sites in flotillin mutants
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by HADA and Van-FL labeling data.

claim: B. subtilis cells elongate and lose organisation of MreB when membrane fluidity is decreased by altering the membrane fatty acid composition.
source: Our findings are also in agreement with the recent observation that B. subtilis cells elongate and lose organisation of MreB when membrane fluidity is decreased by altering the membrane fatty acid composition (Gohrbandt, 2019) (H. Strahl, personal communication).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation and personal communication.

claim: MurG localises to the septum in different organisms.
source: There are several reports that MurG localises to the septum in different organisms (Aaron et al., 2007; Mohammadi et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: A large amount of the peptidoglycan synthesis contributing to elongation of bacterial cells is actually taking place at midcell, before the ingrowth of the septum.
source: one has to remember that a large amount of the peptidoglycan synthesis contributing to elongation of bacterial cells is actually taking place at midcell, before the ingrowth of the septum (Aaron et al., 2007; Pazos et al., 2018; Varma and Young, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: At low growth rates, there is no difference between wild type cells and cells lacking flotillins with respect to membrane fluidity.
source: At low growth rates, there is no difference between wild type cells and cells lacking flotillins with respect to membrane fluidity
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by Laurdan microscopy data on SMM-grown cells.

claim: At low growth rates, the speed of MreB is similar between wild type and flotillin mutant cells.
source: and the speed of MreB is similar between the two cell types.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by TIRF microscopy data on SMM-grown cells.

claim: Although we were capable of detecting a high MW complex containing various PBPs (notably PBP1, 2a, 2b, 3 and 4), the complex was not dependent on the presence of flotillins.
source: Although we were capable of detecting a high MW complex containing various PBPs (notably PBP1, 2a, 2b, 3 and 4), the complex was not dependent on the presence of flotillins.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by 2D BN/SDS-PAGE data.

claim: PBP5 was not part of the high MW complex.
source: PBP5, on the other hand, was not part of the high MW complex
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by 2D BN/SDS-PAGE data.

claim: Our results do not provide any evidence for a role for flotillins in the oligomerisation of PBPs in B. subtilis.
source: Although we cannot exclude that flotillins may affect PBPs that are not easily detected by Bocillin-FL, our results do not provide any evidence for a role for flotillins in the oligomerisation of PBPs in B. subtilis.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the PBP oligomerization experiments.

claim: Peptidoglycan synthesis is altered in the absence of flotillins.
source: Although it is obvious that peptidoglycan synthesis is altered in the absence of flotillins
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by HADA and Van-FL labeling data.

claim: The basis for the alteration in peptidoglycan synthesis in the absence of flotillins is in the physical organisation of the membrane rather than inefficient formation of divisome or elongasome complexes.
source: our data strongly suggest that the basis for this alteration is in the physical organisation of the membrane rather than inefficient formation of divisome or elongasome complexes in the absence of flotillins
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a main conclusion.

claim: Flotillin mutants strains show no synthetic phenotype on minimal medium.
source: because flotillin mutants strains show no synthetic phenotype on minimal medium
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by microscopy data on SMM-grown cells.

claim: The defects on rich medium in flotillin mutants can be reverted by chemically fluidising the membrane.
source: and the defects on rich medium can be reverted by chemically fluidising the membrane.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by benzyl alcohol treatment data.

claim: Flotillins differentially affect the membrane in different growth conditions.
source: The observation that flotillins differentially affect the membrane in different growth conditions also explains the diversity of phenotypes described for flotillin mutants in the literature.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an explanation for literature variability.

claim: A double deletion of floA/floT was reported to suffer severe shape defects and perturbed membrane structure.
source: In previous studies, a double deletion of floA/floT was either reported to suffer severe shape defects and perturbed membrane structure (Dempwolff et al., 2012)
evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation.

claim: A double deletion of floA/floT was reported to not have strong shape defects but with a change in the overall lipid ordering of the membrane.
source: or to not have strong shape defects but with a change in the overall lipid ordering of the membrane (Bach and Bramkamp, 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation.

claim: Simultaneous deletion of pbp1, floA, and floT results in strong filamentation and delocalisation of peptidoglycan synthesis as well as membrane dyes to patches.
source: Simultaneous deletion of pbp1, floA, and floT resulted in strong filamentation and delocalisation of peptidoglycan synthesis as well as membrane dyes to patches (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by microscopy data in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: None of the mutant strains had an apparent phenotype when cultivated in Spizizen's minimal medium (SMM).
source: Strikingly, none of the mutant strains had an apparent phenotype when cultivated in Spizizen's minimal medium (SMM, Figure 2B)
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by microscopy data in Figure 2B.

claim: Peptidoglycan synthesis and lipid dyes are no longer accumulating at division sites in the ΔfloAT strain grown on SMM.
source: and peptidoglycan synthesis and lipid dyes were no longer accumulating at division sites in the ΔfloAT strain (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by microscopy data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The increase in Mg2+ is not sufficient to explain the reversal of phenotype as cells grown on LB supplemented with Mg2+ still display the elongated phenotype with delocalised peptidoglycan synthesis.
source: However, the increase in Mg2+ was not sufficient to explain the reversal of phenotype as cells grown on LB supplemented with Mg2+ (6 mM, concentration in SMM, or 20 mM) still displayed the elongated phenotype with delocalised peptidoglycan synthesis (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by microscopy data in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The phenotypes associated with the absence of flotillins are growth-rate and/or nutrient related.
source: This indicated that the phenotypes associated with the absence of flotillins are growth-rate and/or nutrient related.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from the SMM and Mg2+ experiments.

claim: There are no differences in the overall PBP-profiles of Bocillin-FL labelled wild type or flotillin deletion strains.
source: We ruled out that the peptidoglycan synthesis stress was caused by a change in the folding or complex formation by PBPs in the absence of flotillins, as there were no differences in the overall PBP-profiles of Bocillin-FL labelled wild type or flotillin deletion strains (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Bocillin-FL labeling data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Various PBPs can be found in a high-MW complex (notably PBPs 1, 2, 3 and 4), but complex formation is similar in the ΔfloAT strain.
source: PBP complex formation was analysed using a combination of Native-PAGE and SDS-PAGE with Bocillin-labelled membrane fractions (Trip and Scheffers, 2016) and showed that various PBPs can be found in a high-MW complex (notably PBPs 1, 2, 3 and 4), but that complex formation is similar in the ΔfloAT strain (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by 2D BN/SDS-PAGE data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: None of the five functional GFP-PBPs examined changed their localisation in the ΔfloAT strain.
source: Also, none of the five functional GFP-PBPs examined changed their localisation in the ΔfloAT strain (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: D-Ala-D-Pra incorporation is delocalised in the ∆pbp1ΔfloAT strain, indicating that peptidoglycan synthesis itself is delocalised.
source: D-Ala-D-Pra incorporation was delocalised in the ∆pbp1ΔfloAT strain, indicating that peptidoglycan synthesis itself is delocalised (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by D-Ala-D-Pra labeling data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The accumulation of lipid dyes indicative of increased fluidity at division sites is in line with a recent study that showed phases of different fluidity in Streptococcus pneumoniae membranes, with more fluid membranes and LipidII localising at midcell.
source: The accumulation of lipid dyes indicative of increased fluidity at division sites is in line with a recent study that showed phases of different fluidity in Streptococcus pneumoniae membranes, with more fluid membranes and LipidII localising at midcell (Calvez et al., 2019)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: MreB speed is similar to those reported previously.
source: with MreB speeds similar to those reported previously (Billaudeau et al., 2017; Figure 4, Figure 4—videos 1 and 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation and reference to Figure 4.

claim: The flotillin-associated increase in overall membrane fluidity is important for cell shape control at high growth rates.
source: The GP values indicated that membranes are more ordered when cells are grown on minimal medium, and this suggests that the flotillin-associated increase in overall membrane fluidity is important for cell shape control at high growth rates.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from the Laurdan microscopy data.

claim: Nile-Red labelling at the lateral membrane is the same between wild type and ΔfloAT strains, indicating that there is no difference in dye diffusion between the strains.
source: In this mixed-strain experiment, Nile-Red labelling at the lateral membrane was the same between wild type and ΔfloAT strains, indicating that there is no difference in dye diffusion between the strains (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by microscopy data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The peptidoglycan synthesis stress caused by fosfomycin is not the same as the stress caused by the absence of flotillins.
